Observations:  
- Channel 0 (agent) has large W1 norms only along the leftmost playable column, column 1, rows 1â8. Examples: (r2,c1)=7.10, (r1,c1)=6.48, (r7,c1)=5.22, (r8,c1)=4.68. This strongly suggests the agent is a vertical paddle fixed to the left side.  
- Channel 1 (moving objects) has large weights across the inner playable grid, e.g. max 12.17 at (r6,c3), 10.81 at (r5,c2), 10.66 at (r2,c2), 9.64 at (r7,c2). This looks like a ball moving through the play area, possibly plus an opponent paddle near the right playable column.  
- Channel 2 (reward targets) is concentrated on the right border column 9, rows 1â8: (r6,c9)=0.97, (r2,c9)=0.85, (r4,c9)=0.82, (r5,c9)=0.82, (r7,c9)=0.81. That suggests the scoring/goal region is at the right edge.  
- Channel 3 (obstacles) is high almost only on the outer border, e.g. row 0 and row 9 values around 0.7â0.9, column 0 and column 9 similarly high. No inner maze-like obstacle structure is present.  
- Channel 4 (previous frame) has large weights across the inner grid, e.g. (r8,c5)=13.82, (r1,c5)=10.59, (r7,c4)=9.35, consistent with using previous ball/agent positions to infer motion.  
- Top W1 connections are dominated by channel 1 and channel 4, with some channel 0 connections only at column 1, e.g. unit 11 has (r1,c1,ch0)=2.697; unit 15 has (r1,c1,ch0)=-2.474; unit 21 has (r8,c1,ch0)=2.358.  
- Output layer W3 shows strong up/down structure: row 2 is [0.133, 1.003, 1.898, 0.059, 0.046], strongly favoring action 2/down; row 23 is [1.286, 1.734, -0.953, 1.081, 1.053], favoring action 1/up; row 31 is [0.553, 1.950, 0.123, 0.616, 0.587], strongly favoring action 1/up. Left/right columns are often close to no-op or less differentiated, e.g. row 1 [0.451, 0.607, 0.607, 0.489, 0.489]. Biases b3 are all positive around 0.86â1.26, so there is no strong global action bias.

Reasoning:  
The pattern is not a maze, Pac-Man, Snake, or Breakout. In Breakout the paddle would be at the bottom and the important actions would be left/right. Here the agent is fixed to the left column, the moving object travels across the inner grid, and the reward target is at the right edge. The network strongly uses up/down actions, while left/right are much less important. This is exactly the structure of Pong: a left paddle controlled vertically, a ball moving horizontally, and a scoring region on the right side.

Game: Pong.

Description: The agent controls the left paddle and moves it up or down to intercept the ball. Reward is obtained when the ball passes the opponent/goal area on the right, while letting the ball pass the left paddle presumably gives negative reward.

Confidence: 94%
